Context compression is the art of keeping what matters while discarding what doesn't. When you're working with large language models, context window limits become a real constraint.

The skill of context compression involves maintaining what's important while removing what's unnecessary. When dealing with LLMs, the context window size is a significant limitation.

Context compression means keeping important information and removing unimportant parts. Large language models have context window constraints that limit input size.

The technique of compressing context focuses on preserving essential content while eliminating non-essential text. LLM context windows impose limits on input length.

Compressing context effectively requires keeping critical information and discarding redundant content. Context window limitations in large language models restrict input capacity.
